title: I Asked the Grab CFO About the Future — Here’s What He Said
creator: Couch Investor
source_note: Detailed summary generated from video captions; note: captions garble some names and figures in places
summary: Couch Investor (Neil) interviews Grab CFO Peter Oey. Q3 brought revenue up 30%, record profitability across all businesses and a record 57 million monthly transacting users. The headline is a joint AI-infrastructure plan in Malaysia with SoftBank (about $1bn) and Petros (about $100m; Grab about $750m) targeting 5+ GW, milestone-based, with offtakers the critical next step; Southeast Asia's AI usage is about a tenth of the US for roughly 700 million people. On mobility: record active drivers (up 20% year over year), fuel-cost subsidies, driver loans (over a third of drivers; retention up to 3x; non-performing loans 2.5-2.6%) and EV adoption (18% of rides) keep supply growing without raising rider prices. Deliveries: EBITDA margin 2.7% of GMV heading to 4%+ via fulfilment efficiency and AI routing, ads (about 2% penetration, targeting 3%, about 10x return on ad spend, paid per order) and grocery (growing twice as fast as food), plus Grab Mall. Financial services: deposits $2.7bn, loan book target $6bn by 2028, helped by the Atome buy-now-pay-later acquisition (30,000 retail brands); $500m adjusted EBITDA target by 2028 versus $12m last quarter, group target $1.7bn. Uber has been a shareholder since 2018 with a non-compete in Southeast Asia; autonomous vehicles are nascent (WeRide in Singapore; open to Waymo or Uber). Capital: $5bn net cash; $400m buyback done in September-October, $500m more by September 2027 ($1.75bn total, about 10% of shares). No explicit stock call from Neil.
